extracted.intended_audience: employers, immigration attorneys/representatives, and other stakeholders who prepare and file H-1B registrations and petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards for submitting H-1B registrations and for petitions filed after selection, including how USCIS will weight and select registrations by OEWS wage level, required information on petitions, and process-integrity rules. Focused on compliance with the new weighted selection final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted selection by OEWS wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: When random selection is required, USCIS will weight and select unique beneficiaries with properly submitted registrations generally based on the highest OEWS wage level that the beneficiary’s proffered wage will equal or exceed for the relevant SOC code in the area(s) of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrations assigned wage level IV will be entered into the selection pool four times, those assigned wage level III three times, those assigned wage level II two times, and those assigned wage level I one time. This weighting increases the odds of selection for beneficiaries with proffered wages corresponding to higher wage levels. (The rule applies to registrations or to petitions if the registration process is suspended.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant selection of wage-level box
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must select the box for the highest OEWS wage level ('wage level IV,' 'wage level III,' 'wage level II,' or 'wage level I') that the proffered wage generally equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code in the area of intended employment or otherwise select the appropriate box according to the form instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The wage level box selected on the registration should reflect the proffered wage and determine the wage-level assignment used for weighted selection. USCIS assumes companies will keep current wage rates when submitting registrations or petitions; selecting an inaccurate wage level may affect selection odds and later adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique beneficiary counted only once toward numerical allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each unique beneficiary will only be counted once toward the numerical allocation projections, regardless of how many registrations were submitted for that beneficiary or how many times the beneficiary is entered in the selection pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a beneficiary has multiple registrations, the unique beneficiary will be allotted to the lowest wage level of all registrations submitted on his or her behalf. (This affects projections and how multiple submissions interact with the weighting scheme.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain two-stage selection for advanced degree exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule will maintain the two-stage selection process to keep a higher chance of beneficiaries with a qualifying U.S. master’s degree or higher of being selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For analytic simplicity DHS sometimes combines the pool for the regular cap and the advanced degree exemption in modeling, but the rule itself preserves the two-stage selection that favors holders of qualifying U.S. master's degrees consistent with 8 CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition must match selected registration identifying and position information
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B cap-subject petition filed on behalf of a beneficiary will be required to contain and be supported by the same identifying information and position information, including SOC code, provided in the selected registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See new 8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(iii)(D)(1). A petition inconsistent with the selected registration's identifying/position information may be subject to denial or further scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proffered wage on petition must equal or exceed prevailing wage for corresponding OEWS wage level on LCA
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition will be required to include a proffered wage that equals or exceeds the prevailing wage for the corresponding OEWS wage level in the registration for the SOC code in the area(s) of intended employment as indicated on the LCA used to support the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners will be required to submit evidence of the basis of the wage level selected on the registration as of the date that the registration underlying the petition was submitted. This requirement is intended to ensure consistency between registration wage-level claims and petition evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit evidence of basis for selected wage level (as of registration date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners must submit evidence of the basis of the wage level selected on the registration as of the date that the registration underlying the petition was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This evidence requirement appears on the Form I-129 and the H-1B Data Collection and Filing Fee Exemption Supplement (paper and online e-file) and will increase time burden (estimated 15 minutes per petition). The evidence supports adjudication of the wage-level claim used in selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid registration must represent a bona fide job offer
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS is revising 8 CFR 214.2(h)(10)(ii) to clarify that a valid registration must represent a bona fide job offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrations that do not reflect a bona fide job offer may be subject to denial of subsequent petitions. This standard underpins process integrity and supports USCIS authority to act against registrations intended solely to game the selection system.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS authority to deny petitions that unfairly increase selection odds
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may deny a subsequent new or amended petition filed by the petitioner, or a related entity, on behalf of the same beneficiary if USCIS determines the filing was part of the petitioner’s attempt to unfairly increase the odds of selection during the registration (or petition, if applicable) selection process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include reducing the proffered wage to an amount equivalent to a lower wage level than indicated on the original registration or petition. Attempting to derive the benefit associated with a higher wage level without a bona fide job offer at that wage level generally falls within this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection weight/probability calculation approach (DHS analytic method)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS's analytic formulation for weighted probability: the probability of selection under weighted selection for level I is 15.29% = (94,900 ÷ (89,911 × 1 + 177,216 × 2 + 37,928 × 3 + 15,657 × 4)) × 100%. Level II = 15.29% × 2, Level III = 15.29% × 3, Level IV = 15.29% × 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS notes calculating weighted probability without replacement is complex; for simulation of final impacts DHS used Monte Carlo simulation because simple multiplication of petitions by selection probabilities would overstate impacts. DHS also notes the analytic method assumes employers keep current wage rates when submitting registrations and may underestimate future shifts toward higher wages.

rubrics_metrics.name: If registration suspended, petition selection follows same wage-level weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule will change the way USCIS selects registrations for H-1B cap-subject petitions (or petitions, if the registration process is suspended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All selection-weighting and wage-level assignment rules apply in either case: whether selecting registrations or selecting petitions when registration is suspended, the wage-level-based weighting mechanism governs selection entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple registrations and projections: modeling and counting conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For projections and modeling, DHS counts each unique beneficiary once and redistributes N/A wage-level counts among wage levels using the percent of total; estimated beneficiaries by wage level are estimated using percentages of the 5-year average of beneficiaries with eligible registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These modeling conventions (e.g., redistributing N/A data, using 5-year averages) are used in DHS tables and impact probability and projection outcomes; they inform how impact estimates (e.g., estimated petition receipts, wage-distribution impacts) are computed and presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process-integrity related form changes and burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule adds additional questions for petitioners on Form I-129 and H-1B supplements (paper and online e-file) about wage level information, SOC code, and evidence of the basis for the wage level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS estimates these additional questions increase time burden by 15 minutes per petition and will increase integrity by allowing USCIS to better validate registration and petition consistency. Estimated additional opportunity costs for attorneys and HR specialists are provided in DHS analysis.
